findings.where: Screen 5 (The dots line up), after Dan drags 0.5 in
findings.what: Dropping 0.5 calls play(3.0), which restarts T at 0 and stops the motion at about 3.0 s, but the line (lineT 3.4), its f(x) = 3x − 1 label and the +1/+3 triangle (triT 3.9) are timed from T = 0. So the line and triangle vanish the moment he drops 0.5 and never come back (anim.pause does not repaint at T = Infinity), and the screen that says '0.5 lands on the same line' ends with no line. Draw lineT, triT and flab parts fully once st.demoDone is true, or make the drop's motion end after them.

The brief's lesson 1 promises 'input and output are the independent and dependent variables' (MCA Second Engineer syllabus, 'Defines the dependent and independent variables', notes 3.3), but neither the explain nor any screen names them. Add one sentence, e.g. on screen 3: 'x is the independent variable, the one you choose; f(x) is the dependent variable, because it depends on x.' Or move the point in the brief to lesson 2.

findings.where: Screens 2, 4 and 6 (task text 'Feed 2 into…', 'Drop in −2', 'Drop in a + 1')
findings.what: The prompts tell Dan to drop the token in, but on puzzle screens the token cannot be dragged. It only travels in when he presses Check, so a drag attempt does nothing. Reword, e.g. 'If −2 goes in, what is f(−2)?', or let the drag act as Check.

'f(x) is not f times x' is first said in the hint for the fa + f slip on screen 6. That puzzle tests the idea before any SHOW screen shows it, though the brief makes it lesson 1's main misconception. Add a sentence to screen 3: 'The bracket holds the input; f(5) does not mean f times 5.'

findings.where: Screen 5 text and explain paragraph 3 ('which is why the whole line is drawn')
findings.what: One extra point at 0.5 does not show why every in-between input is on the line. Give the reason the ignores note already states, e.g. 'Any input in between, like 0.5, still has 3 added for each 1 across, so it lands on the same line too; that is why the whole line is drawn.'

findings.where: Explain, paragraph 4 ('The flow meter in the course's puzzle')
findings.what: No puzzle in this lesson is a flow meter. The 4 to 20 mA screen is a transmitter with percent going in, so this sentence points at something Dan has not seen. Reword, e.g. 'The transmitter on a flow meter's pressure cell is a function too: pressure difference in, current out, 12 mA for 50%.'

findings.where: Screen 12 task text at 1280 px (and any number-unit pair in task text)
findings.what: The line wraps between '2' and 'Ω' ('With a 2 / Ω resistor'), which splits a value from its unit. Join number and unit with a no-break space in the task strings ('2\u00a0Ω', '4\u00a0mA', '20\u00a0mA').

findings.where: Screen 6 (Feed in a + 1), right answer: dot label 'a = 2' and table row '3 | 8'
findings.what: The check dot sits at input 3 but is labelled 'a = 2', and its table row '3 | 8' has no label, so it can read as a mismatch until he opens Why?. Label the dot 'a = 2, so 3 in', or mark the row the same way.

findings.where: Screen 1 opening state, the token row
findings.what: The demo's 5 waits in the same row and the same navy style as Dan's own 0 and 1, so it looks like a third token for him to drag, and then it moves by itself. Start it at the funnel's mouth, or give it a lighter look while it waits.

findings.where: Screen 12 (Power in a resistor), Why? text
findings.what: After the right answer the dots (1, 2), (2, 8) and (3, 18) visibly curve, unlike f's straight line, but nothing says so. One clause would use the picture and set up lesson 3: 'These dots do not line up: each extra amp adds more watts than the last. That curve is the square, in lesson 3.'
